name: ISP core
kid: The motorway of your internet company: super-fast connections between big cities.
nerd: An MPLS core with 100–400G links; packets are label-switched rather than looked up at every hop.

1995.name: ISP router
1995.kid: The internet company’s one big router, in a back room. Every parcel from its callers passes through it.
1995.nerd: The small ISP’s one router: Ethernet to the modem bank, a leased E1 to its upstream and another to DIX. It looks up every packet’s address in its table; there were no MPLS labels yet (RFC 3031, 2001).

2010.nerd: An MPLS core with 10–40G links, the first 100G arriving in 2010; packets are label-switched rather than looked up at every hop.
